record.context_brief: Asymptotic lower bound for computing X_alpha
record.original_question: In the linear model where an algorithm for a transformation is a product of matrices R_t and each step R_t is block diagonal with n-2 identity blocks and one 2x2 unitary block acting on only two coordinates, let F be the normalized n x n Fourier transform, let G = [[0, F], [-F^*, 0]], and define X_alpha = (cos alpha) Id + (sin alpha) G on C^(2n). What is the true asymptotic lower bound, as alpha tends to 0, on the number of such two-coordinate unitary steps required to compute X_alpha? In particular, can one prove that computing X_alpha requires essentially Omega(n log n) steps rather than only the currently derived Omega(alpha^2 n log n) or Omega(alpha n log n) lower bounds?

evidence.quote: The work [Ailon(2013)] provides a lower bound of Omega(n log n) operations for computing F x (or Hx) given x, assuming that at each step the computer can perform a unitary operation affecting at most 2 rows.

Consider the 2n x 2n matrix G defined as G = ((0, F), (-F^*, 0)). ... Let Id denote the 2n x 2n identity matrix, and finally define for a real angle alpha the following matrix: X_alpha = (cos alpha) Id + (sin alpha) G.
Hence, we conjecture that the number of steps required to compute X_alpha should be not much smaller than Omega(n log n).
The author conjectures Omega((n log n)/ log(1/alpha)) to be the correct bound.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and let F denote the normalized n×n discrete Fourier transform matrix, i.e. the unitary matrix with entries F_{jk} = (1/√n) exp(2πi jk/n) for 0 ≤ j,k ≤ n−1. Let F* denote its conjugate transpose. Define the 2n×2n unitary block matrix

   G = [[0, F], [−F*, 0]],

and, for a real parameter α, the 2n×2n unitary matrix

   X_α = (cos α) I_{2n} + (sin α) G.

Consider the following linear computational model. An "algorithm" computing a 2n×2n unitary U is a factorization U = R_T R_{T−1} ⋯ R_1, where each R_t is a 2n×2n unitary that is, up to permutation of coordinates, block-diagonal with one nontrivial 2×2 unitary block acting on two coordinates and the identity on the remaining 2n−2 coordinates. The cost of the algorithm is T, the number of such two-coordinate steps. Let c(U) denote the minimum cost over all such factorizations of U.

It is known that c(F) = Ω(n log n), and that c(X_α) ≥ Ω(α² n log n) and c(X_α) ≥ Ω(α n log n) can be established for small α > 0.

Determine the true asymptotic behavior of c(X_α) as α → 0 (with n → ∞). In particular, prove or disprove the conjecture that

   c(X_α) = Ω( (n log n) / log(1/α) ),

and decide whether c(X_α) = Ω(n log n) holds, i.e. whether the dependence on α can be eliminated entirely from the lower bound.
artifact.status_search_result: Obtaining tight super-linear lower bounds for computing Fourier-type unitaries in the 2×2 unitary gate linear model is a longstanding open problem. Ailon's matrix-entropy method gives Ω(n log n) for F itself and Ω((n log n)/R) in R-well-conditioned models, but the conjectured Ω((n log n)/log(1/α)) bound for X_α and the question of whether α-independent Ω(n log n) holds appear not to have been resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: A Lower Bound for Fourier Transform Computation in a Linear Model Over 2x2 Unitary Gates Using Matrix Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: In a layered linear circuit model restricted to unitary 2×2 gates, one obtains an Ω(n log n) lower bound for computing F.
status_evidence.claim: The Ω(n log n) lower bound for the unrestricted Fourier transform F itself is established in this model.

status_evidence.title: An n log n Lower Bound for Fourier Transform Computation in the Well Conditioned Model
status_evidence.snippet: Obtaining a non-trivial (super-linear) lower bound for computation of the Fourier transform in the linear circuit model has been a long standing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds in this model remain a long-standing open problem, with results conditional on conditioning assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Tighter Fourier Transform Lower Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: A factor b speedup implies existence of Ω(n) b-ill conditioned bottlenecks occurring at Ω(n) different steps.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work tightens the trade-offs but does not resolve the unconditional Ω(n log n) bound for X_α.
